narrative_synthesis: The meta is rent anxiety from both sides: renters scared of rent hikes and landlords tired enough to sell. Drafts: (1) a tired-landlord options post that fits Philly deal flow, (2) a 'numbers work today' contrast post, (3) a 'seller financing isn't new' take.

drafts.draft_en:
Tired of being a landlord?

You're not stuck with one option.

You can list it. You can sell it as-is for cash. Or you can sell it and carry the financing, so you get paid every month instead of all at once.

If you own a rental in Philly and you're done, let's talk. No pressure.
drafts.pattern: tired-landlord seller signal (summ3rsinclaire) + rent-anxiety star (MsJamandPickle 44.4k) flipped to the seller side; seller-financing hook (heIpfullandlord 11.2k)
drafts.video_tip: Selfie video on a Philly block of rowhomes, 20-30s. Open with 'Tired of being a landlord?' in the first 2 seconds, then the three options on fingers. No promised prices or timelines.

drafts.draft_en:
Buying a rental because "prices always go up"? ❌

Buying it because the numbers work even if they don't? ✅

Run the deal like it never appreciates. If it still pays you, that's the one.

Appreciation is the bonus, not the plan.
drafts.pattern: X-vs-check contrast (depreciationunc, 6 replies in ~3h) + Grant Cardone 'opportunity since 2008' star for the market-timing debate
drafts.video_tip: Split screen or two cuts, 15-20s: say the wrong reason with a head shake, then the right reason with a nod. Keep text on screen for both lines.

drafts.draft_en:
Seller financing isn't new.

It's one of the oldest ways property changes hands: the owner acts as the bank and gets paid over time.

What's new is how many people just learned to ask.

Ask the seller. Worst case they say no.
drafts.pattern: 'seller financing isn't new' pushback (Abude_al_asaad 1.1k) + 'ASK THE SELLER' star (heIpfullandlord 11.2k)
